info.description: A clickable region on a page, with the pulled-out article text.

editionSku.description: Denormalized from the parent Edition's own sku field at creation time — same reasoning as Page.editionSku.

top.description: % from top of the page image — the overall bounding box across every region this story occupies (see `regions` below), kept for any caller that just needs one rectangle

left.description: % from left of the page image

regions.description: The actual heatmap — an array of { top, left, width, height } (same % units as the fields above), one rectangle per COLUMN this story's text occupies, plus a separate one for the headline if it spans wider than any single column. A single top/left/width/height box was found to be structurally wrong for multi-column stories: it stretches from the leftmost occupied column's left edge to the rightmost's right edge, covering the gutters between columns and any unrelated content sandwiched between them if the columns don't have matching line counts. This is what a reader-facing heatmap overlay should actually render — one highlighted rectangle per entry, not the single top/left/width/height box.

continuesToPage.description: Set when the ingest engine found an explicit jump-line on this story (e.g. 'Turned to Page 39') — the page this story's text continues onto. Confidence is intentionally binary: only set when an explicit marker was found in the text, never guessed from layout alone — a real front-page lead story spanning two pages was found with NO such marker at all, just a headline that grammatically continues; that case is left for an editor to notice and link manually, not auto-linked.

continuesFromPage.description: The reverse of continuesToPage — set when this story's own text opens with an explicit 'Continued from Page N' marker.

source.description: auto_detected hotspots come from the ingest pipeline's text-layout heuristic and are published immediately, not held for review — a deliberate choice prioritizing visibility over pre-publication review; check headline/byline/body/box coordinates after the fact if something looks off, since nothing catches an extraction error before it's live.

detectionConfidence.description: 0–1, only set for auto_detected stories. Low values are more likely to need manual correction.
